# Architectural Boundary Enforcement

Tools that enforce import rules and layered architecture constraints in
Python codebases.

## Tool Landscape

| Tool | Version | Python | License | Approach | Stars |
|------|---------|--------|---------|----------|-------|
| import-linter | — | — | BSD-2 | Declarative contracts | 1,000 [10] |
| tach | 0.34.1 (Apr 2026) | >=3.9 | MIT | Boundary marking (Rust) | — [20] |
| grimp | 3.14 (Dec 2025) | 3.10-3.14 | BSD-2 | Queryable graph library | — [12] |
| Deply | — | — | — | Layer rules | — [35] |
| PyTestArch | — | — | — | Pytest fixtures | — [33] |
| flake8-custom-import-rules | — | — | — | Flake8 plugin | — [counter-discovery] |

Note: dependency-cruiser does NOT support Python — it is JavaScript/TypeScript
only [counter-discovery].

## import-linter

The primary architectural boundary enforcer for Python [9][10]. Built on
grimp for import graph analysis [12]. 1,000 stars, 47 releases, active
maintenance [10].

**Six contract types:**

| Contract | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| Forbidden | Prevent one module set from importing another [9] |
| Protected | Restrict direct imports except for whitelisted modules [9] |
| Layers | Enforce layered architecture (higher depends on lower only) [9] |
| Independence | Ensure modules don't depend on each other in any direction [9] |
| Acyclic Siblings | Eliminate dependency cycles among sibling modules [9] |
| Custom | User-defined architecture rules [9] |

**Configuration:** `.importlinter` file with INI-style sections [9]:

```ini
[importlinter]
root_package = myproject

[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = Layered architecture
type = layers
layers =
    myproject.views
    myproject.services
    myproject.models
```

**CLI:** `lint-imports` validates all contracts and reports violations [9].

**Browser UI:** Includes a browser-based interface for exploring package
architecture [9].

## tach

Rust-based module boundary enforcement with zero runtime impact [20][21].
Python >=3.9 through 3.14, MIT license, active development (v0.34.1,
April 2026) [20].

**Commands:**
- `tach init`: interactively define module boundaries [21]
- `tach check`: verify boundaries and interfaces are respected [21]
- `tach sync`: sync constraints with actual dependencies [21]
- `tach show`: visualize dependency relationships [21]

**Configuration:** `tach.toml` [21]. Supports flagging deprecated
dependencies during transition periods [21]. Integrates with CI/CD, pre-commit
hooks, and VS Code extension [20].

## grimp (standalone)

While primarily used as import-linter's engine, grimp can be used directly
for custom architectural checks [12]. The queryable API supports finding
shortest import chains, tracking line numbers, and analyzing multiple root
packages [12].

## Deply

Architecture enforcer that collects code elements into layers via rules
(e.g., `class_inherits`, `decorator_usage`, `file_regex`) and enforces
coupling policies [35].

## PyTestArch

Pytest-based approach using fixtures (`evaluable`, `layered_architecture`)
to test architecture constraints as part of the test suite [33].

## Counter-perspectives

- Architectural enforcement can be overkill for small projects — "90% of
  the benefits with 10% of the complexity" is achievable without formal
  tooling [counter-discovery]
- import-linter's root_package must be importable; external packages are
  not statically analyzed [counter-discovery]
- Dynamic imports and lazy loading (PEP 690) break static analysis
  guarantees [54]
- No architecture erosion control technique is completely effective at
  preventing drift [counter-discovery]
- For teams with high change frequency across boundaries, enforcement
  overhead may exceed benefit [counter-discovery]

## Gaps and Limitations

- import-linter requires the analyzed package to be importable [counter-discovery]
- tach is Beta status (0.x versioning) despite active development [20]
- No tool handles dynamic imports or runtime-generated module paths
- Deply and PyTestArch have limited documentation and adoption data
- flake8-based approaches are limited to single-file analysis scope
